findings.explanation: All three extensions materialize the reified T as T::class.java. getTypeHint<T>() selects Java getTypeHint(Class<?>), which converts the Class to a TypeReference and performs the lookup. The customizer form selects registerType(Class<?>, Consumer<Builder>); noinline permits the bound typeHint::invoke adapter, which passes the Java Builder to the original Kotlin callback. The category form uses *memberCategories, passing the vararg elements to registerType(Class<?>, MemberCategory...), which forwards them to the TypeReference overload and TypeHint.builtWith rather than treating the array as one category.

Both Class-based registration overloads first reject a null Class with Assert.notNull, which throws IllegalArgumentException. Their only subsequent Class guard is a non-null canonical name; a Class without one is silently skipped and this is returned. Thus the customizer is not called for either a null Class or a canonical-name-less Class. For a valid Class, the appropriate TypeReference overload is reached and the customizer runs there. Primitive and array classes are not separately rejected if their canonical names are non-null.

Repeated registration under an equal TypeReference key—TypeReference equality is canonical-name based—reuses the same Builder. The category overload supplies TypeHint.builtWith, whose Builder.withMembers adds all categories to a HashSet: registrations therefore accumulate as set union, retaining earlier categories and collapsing duplicates. The builder is inserted by computeIfAbsent before the customizer is invoked. Because accept has no catch or rollback, a thrown exception propagates while the map entry remains; previously accumulated categories and any categories added before the throw remain. For a newly encountered type, even a throw before category mutation leaves an entry whose category set is empty.

getTypeHint(Class<?>) unconditionally calls TypeReference.of(type), then the TypeReference overload reads the map and returns null when a valid type has no entry; lookup does not create one. In contrast, registering an absent valid type creates its builder and invokes the registration callback. TypeReference.of(Class<?>) delegates to ReflectionTypeReference.of, which validates both the Class and its canonical name with Assert.notNull. Consequently lookup with null Class throws IllegalArgumentException for "'type' must not be null", and lookup for a Class with no canonical name throws IllegalArgumentException for "'type.getCanonicalName()' must not be null". Registration validates null Class directly but silently skips a non-null Class lacking a canonical name.

Each lookup builds a new TypeHint from the retained Builder. Set.copyOf makes that TypeHint's member-category set an unmodifiable snapshot, so a TypeHint returned earlier—and the set returned by its getMemberCategories()—does not change when the same type is registered again. A later lookup builds another TypeHint and observes the builder's newly accumulated category union.
